messages:
eli: Heads-up — trying to install the Python SDK on an M1 Mac and pip fails with wheel/typing issues. `pip install redwood-sdk==0.9.1` pulls a wheel built for manylinux2014_x86_64 only, so pip falls back to sdist and then build isolation fails in some CI setups. mypy also complains because py.typed seems missing from the package.

eli: Repro steps: macOS 12.6 on arm64, pyenv 3.11.6, venv activated, then `pip install redwood-sdk==0.9.1` -> error:
```
ERROR: redwood_sdk-0.9.1-cp311-cp311-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl is not supported on this platform.
Building wheels for collected packages: redwood-sdk
  Building wheel for redwood-sdk (pyproject.toml) ... error
  ERROR: Failed building wheel for redwood-sdk
  Running setup.py clean for redwood-sdk
Failed to build redwood-sdk
ERROR: Could not build wheels for redwood-sdk which use PEP 517 and cannot be installed directly
```

eli: Also getting mypy/IDE warnings: "package is missing or has no py.typed marker" on redwood_sdk.async_client. Our libs check for typed packages so this blocks strict-type checkers.

marco: Thanks — can you paste `pip debug --verbose`? Also which installer did you use to publish that release (wheel tags in CI)? Sounds like wheel was only built for x86_64.

eli: pip debug output snippet:
```
pip: 23.2.1
sys_platform: darwin
machine: arm64
supported tags: (macosx_11_0_arm64, cp311-cp311), (macosx_11_0_universal2, cp311-cp311) ...
```

anya: Quick workaround: `pip install --no-use-pep517 redwood-sdk==0.9.1` sometimes helps if sdist can be installed with legacy setup, but that isn't ideal. Another temporary option: `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk.git@main#egg=redwood-sdk` which pulls a wheel built in GitHub actions (we have arm64 matrix there).

lisa: Oof — thanks for reporting. This lines up with a CI regression where the macOS job that builds universal2 wheels was skipped due to an OS matrix typo. I'll open a patch. Also I'll add a small packaging fix: include py.typed in the MANIFEST so type checkers see the package.

eli: Awesome — thx. For the py.typed fix: mypy requires either a `py.typed` file at package root or type stubs packaged. We're missing that in the wheel from 0.9.1. IDEs like PyCharm won't mark as typed without it.

marco: Also flagging that editable installs (`poetry install --editable .`) behave oddly if pyproject.lock and build-backend isolation interact — some CI using `pip install --editable .` got a different set of deps than `poetry install`. Might be a churn between PEP 517 build isolation and our build backend (flit vs setuptools). We should standardize on one backend in pyproject and add `build` CI step to verify wheels for mac/arm/universal2 + manylinux.

anya: For users blocked by mypy: temp workaround in pyproject toml is to add `mypy.ini` ignore: `[mypy-redwood_sdk.*]\nignore_missing_imports = True` but that's ugly. Better to ship py.typed.

lisa: I'll push a tiny PR which: (1) ensures MANIFEST.in includes `redwood_sdk/py.typed`, (2) adjusts GitHub Actions to build universal2 mac wheels on macos-12 and macos-13 runners, (3) publishes a v0.9.2 with both wheel tags and the py.typed.

eli: Will try the git+https install in the meantime and report back. Also, FYI: some customers hit this when adding redwood-sdk to a constraints file for fleet images — sdist-only caused long build times. A wheel matrix is important.

devex-bot: Created GH issue #2345: "packaging: publish mac/arm wheels and include py.typed in package" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/2345 :white_check_mark:

marco: Perfect. Once lisa's PR lands we'll cut 0.9.2 and ping the release channel. Thanks for the clear repro, eli.

eli: Thanks — feel free to assign me to the issue if you want an extra test on M1. :thumbsup:
